newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call rates slip, gilt volumes on NSE rise.
newsitem.headline: Indian call rates slip, gilt volumes on NSE rise.

text.p: Indian call money closed at 8.00-8.50 percent on Tuesday, down from the day's opening of 9.75-10.00 percent, dealers said.
A dealer at Discount and Finance House of India (DFHI) said
The market opened at 9.75 percent and soon dropeed to 9.25 percent, a dealer at Discount and Finance House of India said.
She said the market came down below 9 percent for small volume transactions and towards the close it firmed up to 9.25 percent levels.

There was very little activity in the securities market, a dealer at state run bank said. The zero coupon bond was active as the secondary market yield is much better than the primary market yield for the bond sold by the Reserve Bank of India on Monday, Vinod Dikshit of Centurion Bank said.

He said the 13.50 percent maturing in 1998 saw some selling presure from foreign banks who wanted to avoid the tax on the coupon, while the state-run banks were buying these securities as they are exempted from tax.
Foreign banks are charged at 55 percent on amount of coupon while banks other than state-owned are charged at about 23-24 percent, dealers said.
Jatin Thakkar at Mukesh Babu Securities Ltd said the National Stock Exchange recorded trades worth 1.40 billion rupees on Tuesday against 982.10 million rupees on Monday.

He said the 13.50 percent 1997 was traded at 12.95 percent, slightly up from the Monday's level of 12.94 percent, while 13.50 percent 1998 was traded at 13.36 percent against Monday's level of 13.34 percent. the 13.82 percent 2002 remained

Inter-corporate deposit rates were steady at 18-20 percent for blue-chip companies and certificate of deposits (CD) of financial institutions were traded above 13.25 percent levels, Bharti Anand at SMIFS International Finance said.
